title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
why_read: An interesting approach to distilling LLM-based natural language specs into small, fast, deployable neural functions instead of calling a remote model each time.
analysis: This paper proposes 'compile by training': using a large teacher model to generate synthetic training data that trains a small adapter/interpreter to replicate a natural-language-specified function locally, avoiding per-call latency and cost of a hosted LLM. It reports 83.6% semantic accuracy on a hard benchmark subset with compile times around a minute, and demonstrates real deployed use-cases like a translator and 3D avatar controller. This is technically interesting for engineers thinking about cost/latency tradeoffs in LLM-powered features and distillation-as-compilation as a paradigm.
